items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: We had some in the band. Thornton Blue was one of the best clarinet players in those days, Professor Blue's son.

ctx.x: So you were playing professionally about what year? Well professionally I would say back

I was 18, 19, 18, because I used to play with a three piece group out in a roadhouse, go out on the outskirts of St. Louis and play in what we call nightclub, roadhouses, and have piano, drums, and trumpet. That day there was a bunch of them saxophone, saxophone was just coming through then. Did you ever play with clarinet? Not often because clarinet players were very slow in that day. They didn't have too many clarinet players in St. Louis? No. We had some in the band. Thornton Blue was one of the best clarinet…
Did you ever get outside St. Louis in those years to play? Did you get jobs on the road?
